notes: Chained model-serving build: implement two hand-rolled tensor-parallel linear layers (row-parallel shards the input dimension and all-reduces partial sums; column-parallel shards the output dimension and all-gathers, with sharded gradients that must match an unsharded dense reference), then build and train a two-head forward engine (policy_logits + post-softmax value) on top of them, then stand up a Flask /classify endpoint with the documented schema. dependent_stages=3: the PolicyWDLEngine forward relies on the parallel layers being numerically correct; the trained checkpoint is what the hidden --infer runs reuse; the /classify endpoint is a separate serving stage. quantitative_correctness=3 because the forward outputs and sharded gradients of the parallel layers must match a dense linear to ~1e-4 and the check is genuinely independent (verified by cross-checking the solver's printed row output against an independently rebuilt dense reference on a hidden input tensor). adversarial_inputs=3: hidden cases probe nondivisible world partitions (input and output dims), malformed/non-JSON /classify requests, a bad-shape --infer array, and an empty inference batch. hidden_case_generalization=3: the same /app/solve.py runs --validate-parallel over a fresh hidden (in,out,world,seed) numeric case and --infer over a fresh unlabeled feature set the agent has never seen. The reasoning floor is set by implementing correct sharded gradients for the parallel layers which are a genuine interior-stage correctness problem.
